Filter taxa based on across-sample OTU abundance criteria

Source: R/filter_taxa.R
step_filter_taxa.Rd

Add a preprocessing step that applies one safely serializable predicate to each taxon's abundance vector across samples. Filtering is performed during prep(); taxa for which the predicate returns FALSE are removed.

Usage

step_filter_taxa(rec, .f, id = rand_id("filter_taxa"))

Arguments

rec

A Recipe object. The step will be added to the sequence of operations for this Recipe.

.f

A function with exactly one argument named x, without a default, or a character string containing that function expression. It must return a single logical value for the abundance vector x. Only the restricted expression syntax described below is accepted; lists of functions are not supported.

id

A character string that is unique to this step to identify it.

Value

A Recipe with the filtering step added. The constructor does not filter the data or return a logical vector. During prep(), the step uses phyloseq::filter_taxa() with prune = TRUE; there is no prune argument in this wrapper.

Details

The predicate body must be a single expression, without braces, assignments, external variables or user-defined helper calls. Write thresholds as literal numbers inside the expression, even when using the function directly in R. These restrictions keep recipes safely exportable and importable; they are checked when the step is added, not just on export.

Accepted expressions use x, finite numeric or non-missing logical literals, parentheses, arithmetic operators (+, -, *, /, ^, %%, %/%), comparisons (>, >=, <, <=, ==, !=), logical operators (&, |, !), and calls to sum, length, mean, median, min, max, var, sd, any, all or is.na. The only supported named argument is na.rm in sum, mean, median, min, max, var, sd, any and all. Namespace-qualified calls are not accepted.

See also

Other filter phy steps: step_filter_by_abundance(), step_filter_by_prevalence(), step_filter_by_rarity(), step_filter_by_variance()

Examples

data(metaHIV_phy)

## Keep taxa present in at least 3% of samples
recipe(metaHIV_phy) |>
  step_filter_taxa(.f = function(x) sum(x > 0) >= 0.03 * length(x)) |>
  prep()
#> ── DAR Results ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> Inputs:
#> 
#>      ℹ phyloseq object with 279 taxa and 156 samples 
#>      ✖ undefined analysis target. Use add_model() to define the analysis! 
#>      ✖ undefined taxonomic level. Use add_model() to define the analysis! 
#> Results:
#> 

## The same predicate can be supplied as a string
recipe(metaHIV_phy) |>
  step_filter_taxa(.f = "function(x) sum(x > 0) >= 0.03 * length(x)")
#> ── DAR Recipe ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> Inputs:
#> 
#>      ℹ phyloseq object with 451 taxa and 156 samples 
#>      ✖ undefined analysis target. Use add_model() to define the analysis! 
#>      ✖ undefined taxonomic level. Use add_model() to define the analysis! 
#> Preprocessing steps:
#> 
#>      ◉ step_filter_taxa() id = filter_taxa__Cannoli_siciliani 
#> 
#> DA steps:
#>
